defaults.permitted_development: An internal garage conversion in Scotland will often avoid planning permission if it leaves the outside largely unchanged and does not create a separate dwelling. External alterations, enlargement or a planning condition can change that answer.

rules.height_rules: A conversion within the existing garage shell does not create a new height allowance. Any raised roof, new upper floor or rebuilt garage would need separate planning assessment.
rules.depth_rules: The simplest case is an internal fit-out within the existing envelope. Once the project extends the garage, projects outward or materially enlarges the building, it needs to be assessed as new external development.
rules.boundary_rules: Check whether the garage was retained for parking by an earlier permission and review any neighbour-facing or road-facing external changes carefully. Those local conditions often decide the real route.
rules.roof_rules: If the conversion also alters the roof, that roof work needs its own planning assessment. A simple internal fit-out does not itself create a separate roof allowance.
rules.materials_rules: Any infill where the garage door is removed should be designed as part of the house rather than as a patched opening. Conservation area or listed-building controls can still tighten the design response.

rules.permitted_development: A simple internal garage conversion can often proceed in Scotland without planning permission where the existing shell is retained and the outside is not materially altered. Enlargements, visible external changes or separate living use need a fuller review.

rules.height_rules: Garage conversion does not create a fresh height allowance in Scotland. The moment the scheme raises the roof or materially rebuilds the structure, it stops being a simple internal conversion.
rules.depth_rules: Depth is not the main Scottish garage-conversion test. Keeping the work inside the existing shell is usually easiest, while any outward growth moves the scheme into new external development.
rules.boundary_rules: The main Scottish local checks are often parking retention, frontage design and neighbour-facing openings. Even a simple garage-door infill can become contentious where the altered elevation is prominent.
rules.roof_rules: Garage conversion on its own does not open a separate roof right in Scotland. Any proposal to lift, rebuild or materially alter the roof should be treated as external development in its own right.
rules.materials_rules: When a garage door is replaced, aim for materials and detailing that belong with the rest of the house. Frontage changes are usually what attract the closest Scottish design scrutiny.

restrictions.conservation_area: In Aberdeen, conservation area and site-specific conditions can mean external alterations need planning permission even when the internal conversion itself would not.
restrictions.listed_building: Listed building consent may be needed in Aberdeen for internal or external works affecting the character of a listed building or related curtilage structure.
restrictions.article4_notes: No borough-wide Article 4 note is recorded here, but site-specific directions or planning conditions can still remove permitted development rights on particular properties.

rules.permitted_development: In Scotland, works that do not materially affect the external appearance of the building are not normally treated as development, so a straightforward internal garage conversion is often the simplest case. A separate dwelling or obvious external change is different.

rules.height_rules: There is no separate Scottish garage-conversion height right. Once the roofline is lifted, rebuilt or given an extra storey, treat that element as external development in its own right.
rules.depth_rules: There is no dedicated garage-conversion projection right in Scotland. Staying within the existing footprint is the low-risk route; any outward extension or linked enlargement has to be considered separately.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary and frontage issues usually come from the external alterations rather than the internal fit-out. Also check whether an earlier permission required the garage or parking arrangement to be retained.
rules.roof_rules: Roof changes are not part of the ordinary internal-conversion question. Once the scheme includes a raised roof or visible roof alteration, assess that work separately.
rules.materials_rules: The external treatment of a former garage opening matters more than the internal fit-out. A well-matched infill wall, window or door usually reads best, especially on a street-facing elevation.

rules.height_rules: There is no separate Scottish garage-conversion height right. Once the roofline is lifted, rebuilt or given an extra storey, treat that element as external development in its own right.
rules.depth_rules: There is no dedicated garage-conversion projection right in Scotland. Staying within the existing footprint is the low-risk route; any outward extension or linked enlargement has to be considered separately.
rules.boundary_rules: Boundary and frontage issues usually come from the external alterations rather than the internal fit-out. Also check whether an earlier permission required the garage or parking arrangement to be retained.
rules.roof_rules: Roof changes are not part of the ordinary internal-conversion question. Once the scheme includes a raised roof or visible roof alteration, assess that work separately.
rules.materials_rules: The external treatment of a former garage opening matters more than the internal fit-out. A well-matched infill wall, window or door usually reads best, especially on a street-facing elevation.

rules.permitted_development: An internal garage conversion in Scotland will often avoid planning permission if it leaves the outside largely unchanged and does not create a separate dwelling. External alterations, enlargement or a planning condition can change that answer.

rules.height_rules: A conversion within the existing garage shell does not create a new height allowance. Any raised roof, new upper floor or rebuilt garage would need separate planning assessment.
rules.depth_rules: The simplest case is an internal fit-out within the existing envelope. Once the project extends the garage, projects outward or materially enlarges the building, it needs to be assessed as new external development.
rules.boundary_rules: Check whether the garage was retained for parking by an earlier permission and review any neighbour-facing or road-facing external changes carefully. Those local conditions often decide the real route.
rules.roof_rules: If the conversion also alters the roof, that roof work needs its own planning assessment. A simple internal fit-out does not itself create a separate roof allowance.
rules.materials_rules: Any infill where the garage door is removed should be designed as part of the house rather than as a patched opening. Conservation area or listed-building controls can still tighten the design response.

rules.permitted_development: A simple internal garage conversion can often proceed in Scotland without planning permission where the existing shell is retained and the outside is not materially altered. Enlargements, visible external changes or separate living use need a fuller review.

rules.height_rules: Garage conversion does not create a fresh height allowance in Scotland. The moment the scheme raises the roof or materially rebuilds the structure, it stops being a simple internal conversion.
rules.depth_rules: Depth is not the main Scottish garage-conversion test. Keeping the work inside the existing shell is usually easiest, while any outward growth moves the scheme into new external development.
rules.boundary_rules: The main Scottish local checks are often parking retention, frontage design and neighbour-facing openings. Even a simple garage-door infill can become contentious where the altered elevation is prominent.
rules.roof_rules: Garage conversion on its own does not open a separate roof right in Scotland. Any proposal to lift, rebuild or materially alter the roof should be treated as external development in its own right.
rules.materials_rules: When a garage door is replaced, aim for materials and detailing that belong with the rest of the house. Frontage changes are usually what attract the closest Scottish design scrutiny.
